approach: Root cause, worded identically in new decision D189 and the CHANGELOG entry: criteria are checked independently only after the producer ends, so an unmet criterion found by the verifier cannot trigger a repair. `produce_and_verify` (run/mod.rs:1871-1950) runs one producer loop, one candidate, one set of checks and one verifier, and a fail verdict closes the job Rejected. Only the producer's own report is ever sent back (`unmet_criteria`, run/send_back.rs:19, used at producer.rs:465). What is missing is the independent verdict reaching the producer while a round is left to use it. Fix, in the run pipeline, bounded, no refusal rule (0% of past accepted readings newly refused): (a) move one round (snapshot, producer loop, candidate, `Built`, resume mark, `check_and_verify`) into `produce_round`; (b) after round one a pure `verify::repair_view(&Verification) -> Option<RepairView>` reads the stored verdict and is Some only when the verifier judged, the verdict is Fail and a repairable unmet criterion or blocker/major finding is left; (c) while fewer than the new `VERIFIER_REPAIRS` (=1, beside `PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS`, mod.rs:1681) repairs have run, not nested, and `preflight(Run)` and the disk gate pass, run round two from a snapshot seeded with the first candidate, whose brief is built by `send_back_text_repaired`, the new last link of the existing send-back chain; (d) the round-two verdict is final; a round two that stops with no verdict restores round one's candidate, Verification, happened state and files and closes Rejected exactly as it would have without the repair. Answers to the round-4 findings. Findings 1 and 2 (minor, files outside the deliverables): kept, each justified below (decision 7): `finding_text` needs one token of visibility (retry.rs:446 is `pub(super)`, so `crate::reading::finding_text` is not nameable from verify.rs without it) and the drain test at drain.rs:5204-5253 counts producer entries and necessarily changes when a failing verdict repairs; both are under the request's `Files: crates/`. Finding 3 (major): the scope guard is now a listed dependent and has a decision (decision 6): a repaired attempt is one attempt for T1 and T4 and its two-round spend and wall time count in full toward T3 and T5 (`attempt_of` sums every non-reader invocation, scope_guard.rs:698-706); thresholds are not retuned (scope_guard.rs:32); a repaired attempt that lands is `done`, so T3 and T5 give None; the scope_guard.rs test rig pops one verdict per Verifier call (scope_guard.rs:1353, 1512) and is changed in a stated way, with two new pins. Finding 4 (minor): the forecast and calibration readers are named in dependents (`score_records`, `scoring::history`, `reference_forecast`, `class_forecasts`) and D189 and the CHANGELOG say a repaired job's actual cost and time include both rounds and `verification_passes` resolves on the final verdict; forecasts themselves are unchanged. Finding 5 (minor): D189 says a repaired job that passes keeps the first verdict only as text in the first verifier invocation's `detail`, and names a typed first-round record as possible follow-up. Finding 6 (minor): the nested-run guards in run/mod.rs are `self.nested.is_none()` at lines 1980, 2006 and 2028 (the grep for `is_some()` finds the other two uses, at 1800 and 2534); the plan cites those and adds the same guard to the repair loop.

decisions.choice: Repair loop wraps one round in `produce_and_verify`; the trigger is the pure `verify::repair_view` over the stored `Verification`, not a new field carried out of `verification_stage`. Round two reuses the whole round: snapshot seeded with the first candidate, producer loop, candidate stage, checks, replay, verifier.
decisions.reason: Everything the trigger needs is already stored: `agent_verdict` is Some exactly when the verifier returned output (verify.rs:639-645), a timeout or incomplete verifier leaves it None, and `Finding.source` and `CriterionResult.evidence` carry what is needed to spot Athena's own findings (verify.rs:292-299, 541-555, 600-604, 629-633). Reusing the round keeps admission, the decision gate, the checks, the replay and the pull-request replace identical for the second candidate. A `closing.verification` that is Some after round two means a verdict was reached, because round one's is taken out before round two and the early stops in `check_and_verify` (mod.rs:1979-2056) and the `candidate_stage` stops return with it None. Existing code already treats a misread and an unmet or unseen Behavior criterion as not retryable from the tree (`qualifies_for_tree_retry`, retry.rs:347-359), so the exclusions match what the repo already means by 'a producer pass cannot fix it'.

A hold (Err) is left to `commit_hold`. A repaired job that passes keeps the first verdict only as text in the first verifier invocation's `detail` (every unmet criterion and blocking finding, no count cap, each clipped to 240 chars, plus 'sent back to the producer for one repair pass'); D189 says so and names a typed first-round record (a second Verification path or a typed Invocation field) as possible follow-up work.

Without the restore a repaired job whose second producer fails would close Failed with no Verification, and `tree_retry_seed` returns None without one (retry.rs:410-412). `closing.files` is written before close only at mod.rs:1008, mod.rs:2264-2268 (replay record) and verification.rs:201 (`brief-verifier.md`), so restoring the cloned `files` removes the stale note and puts round one's replay and verifier brief back. Round two's invocations stay in `new_invocations`. With the restore the job ends where it ended before this change: Rejected with the first candidate and verifier findings. A deadline, expired login, usage limit, check timeout or any producer, admission, gate or scope stop in round two is classed as the first verdict standing, not an environment stop, and uses no attempt the first verdict had not used (Rejected is never resumable: `resumable_stop`, disk.rs:537-543; `keeps_unfinished_work`, disk.rs:549-557). `Closing::put_file` (remove same-path files, then push) is used for the replay record and `brief-verifier.md` so a round that reaches a verdict replaces round one's. The stored first verdict survives only as the detail text because the Verification path is per job (records.rs:934) and a second one needs an athena-data record or allow-list change, which this job does not make. When round two reaches a verdict, a fail has reason `the final verdict is fail: {second reasons}. {note}`; a restored first round has `the final verdict is fail: {first reasons}. {note}; the repair pass stopped before a verdict: {round two's stop reason}`. The prefix `the final verdict is fail:` stays first (close.rs:53); the note is redacted. The introspector builds `what` from `outcome.reason` plus `failure_details(verification)` and does not read `Invocation.detail` (introspect.rs:1538-1572), so the reason carries all first-round items.

decisions.choice: The repair brief extends the existing builder chain: `send_back_text_scoped` becomes a wrapper over a new last link `send_back_text_repaired(.., repair: Option<&RepairView>)`, and the same `Option<&RepairView>` is passed into `producer_loop`, which uses it for its first attempt brief and its own send-backs (the four-arm match at producer.rs:684-700 becomes one call). With None the text is byte-identical. With Some, one `## Sent back` heading holds the repair intro (it replaces the 'Your previous report...' paragraph) then the lists. The first sentence of the intro is a pub const `REPAIR_LEAD` in briefs.rs, so tests and the scope-guard rig can tell a repair prompt apart from any other.
decisions.reason: The shared intro is false for a repair: 'your previous report did not show every criterion met', 'This is the only send-back' and 'A run that leaves no change fails' (send_back.rs:162-173); a seeded run that adds nothing is the candidate, not an idle producer (candidate.rs:168-181). The base snapshot text says 'a snapshot of the base commit's files' (briefs.rs:710-714) while the seeded one is the base plus the candidate's files laid over it, uncommitted (snapshot.rs:97-101). The intro states four facts: the directory is a fresh snapshot already holding the first candidate (`git diff` against its base shows it); the independent verifier, not the producer's report, found the items; a run that adds nothing keeps the first candidate and it is verified again unchanged; the verdict after this round is final. `producer_loop` builds its own send-back from the `brief` it is given (producer.rs:684-700), so a round-two brief that was already a repair text would hold two `## Sent back` headings; passing the view in keeps one heading, and items from the producer's own report in this round are listed under the existing headings after the repair intro (`append_mirror_drift`, send_back.rs:227-247, still finds one heading). The findings block is shared with `must_address_block` (briefs.rs:616-629) and each finding is formatted by `finding_text` (retry.rs:446), so a finding reads the same in a retry and in a repair; texts pass through `ctx.redactor` as `tree_retry_seed` does (retry.rs:424).

decisions.choice: Trigger and exclusions in `repair_view`: a judged Fail verdict with an unmet criterion or a blocker or major finding, minus (i) a criterion whose evidence is the not-assessed text and its Athena 'Criterion N was not assessed' finding; (ii) the Athena request-misread finding; (iii) only when `agent_verdict` is Pass, the Athena D43 findings ('Behavior criterion N is unmet: ... must cite commands that ran (D43)') and the criteria they name. With `agent_verdict` Fail the D43 items stay in. Recognisers are shared consts in verify.rs (`NOT_ASSESSED_EVIDENCE`, `MISREAD_SUMMARY`, `NOT_ASSESSED_SUFFIX`, `D43_PREFIX`, `D43_SUFFIX`); `judge` uses the first two for its non-`format!` literals (verify.rs:544, 631) and keeps both `format!` literals (552, 602) where they are.
decisions.reason:
`judge` fails the verdict on exactly these items (verify.rs:646-664). Not-assessed (549-555) and misread (627-634) describe what the verifier did or read, and nothing a producer pass changes decides them. The D43 flip sets `met = false` where the verifier's cited commands were not seen running or it cited none (585-605), and the stored record loses the verifier's own `met`. When the verifier's verdict is Pass every unmet or blocking D43 item is Athena's flip, so a producer pass cannot fix it. When it is Fail the verifier itself found a fault, often in that same criterion, so the repair runs. Known cost: a Fail whose only serious items are D43 flips spends one round the producer may not be able to change; bounded to one round, not measured, named in D189 and the CHANGELOG. A failing check repairs only through the verifier: `judge` adds a Minor finding for a failing check (verify.rs:448-473) and the check blocks a pass at verify.rs:663, so a verdict that marks the check criterion unmet, or adds a blocker or major finding, repairs; a failing check the verifier did not flag triggers none. Athena's own blockers and majors a producer can fix (held replay, a requirement row marked Covered) stay in. Keeping the `format!` literals inside `judge` leaves `drift_haystack` (verify.rs:3881-3920, which reads only `//!` header lines and `format!(` literals between `
pub fn judge(` and the next `
}
`) and its tests (3923-3945) unchanged.

rejected.why: Repairs a misread or an unassessed criterion at full cost with no way to change the outcome.

rejected.option: Trigger on a failed check as well
rejected.why: The producer already had one send-back with the check's output tail before the verifier; the verifier's unmet check criterion already triggers a repair.

rejected.why: Misses a criterion the verifier itself judged unmet that cites no command; `agent_verdict` Fail is a stored signal that narrows the gap.

decisions.choice: Scope guard and forecast readers: a repaired job is one attempt; its two-round spend and wall time count in full toward T3 and T5, and no signal, threshold, forecast or measure code changes. D189 and the CHANGELOG say so. Tests: the scope_guard.rs test rig reads one queue entry per job (a failing entry is repeated by the verifier in the repair round, unless a `repair_passes` switch is set), and two new pins show the repaired spend and the repaired landing.
decisions.reason: `attempt_of` takes `cost_dollars` from `totals.cost_execution` (scope_guard.rs:698-702), which sums every non-reader invocation (scoring.rs:116-119), and `agent_minutes` from `wall_time_execution` (scope_guard.rs:703-706), which is the run clock from dispatch to the final verdict (verification.rs:457; mod.rs:2586), so both rounds are in the figure whichever way T3 reads it; discounting the repair would need tagging invocations and a measure change, and every threshold is already marked an estimate to be tuned (scope_guard.rs:32). Intended effect: a rejected repaired attempt, which really spent about twice a single round, reaches T3 flag (1.0 x p90) or pause (1.5 x p90, scope_guard.rs:423-428) after fewer attempts than before; a near-complete rejection still gets its one targeted retry (`near_complete`, :300; `targeted_retry`, :314), and an attempt that lands after the repair is `done`, so T3 and T5 return None (:419, :471). T1 and T4 are unchanged: a job is one attempt (T1, :329) and T4 reads the first unmet criterion of the final Verification (:685-689). `progress_of` and `gaps_only` (:721-780) read the stored final Verification: round two's when it reached a verdict, round one's after a restore. For forecasts: `score_records` resolves `verification_passes` on the final verdict (athena-score lib.rs:447-448), `cost_usd` on the sum of every non-reader invocation (453-457, 485-487) and `wall_time_s` on the dispatch-to-verdict time (490), and `scoring::history` (scoring.rs:14-50) feeds those actuals to `reference_forecast` (lib.rs:140-170); so a repaired job's actuals include both rounds and its `verification_passes` is true when round two passes. The reader forecast itself is whatever the reader writes and is left unchanged.

rejected.why: Needs a way to tag repair invocations in athena-data records and a change to a measure; the spend is real and the thresholds are estimates to be tuned.

rejected.why: Its rig pops one verdict per Verifier call (scope_guard.rs:1512), so with a repair the verdict sequence across jobs shifts and the T4 and T3 tests fail (the second job would pass); they must change.

risks.risk: Many existing tests (run/tests.rs, scope_guard.rs, athena-cli) use a fixed failing verdict and assume one producer and one verifier run, so the blast radius is larger than the 11 listed deliverables.
risks.mitigation: Step 11 runs the whole workspace suite right after the core change, so the real list is found by `cargo test --locked`. Each assertion that counted one round gets new counts, costs or a script answer for the second call. The scope_guard rig rule and the drain test are planned by name; lifecycle.rs:641-731 and introspection.rs:421-471 should pass because the retry brief reads only the final Verification and `what` still holds the final verification's items. Athena flags files outside the listed deliverables as minor and the plan accepts that.

risks.risk: Cost: a repaired job pays for a second producer pass, checks (with their timeouts) and verifier, and holds the build-folder slot one round longer. With D43 items repairable on a verifier Fail, some repairs may be rounds the producer cannot change.
risks.mitigation: The bound is a named constant, tested at exactly one repair. `preflight(Run)` skips a repair the job budget cannot pay for. D189 and the CHANGELOG give the worst case from the code (up to 3 producer runs per round, so 6; up to 4 verifier runs), labelled an estimate; the extra wall time, cost per repaired job and the share of D43-only repairs are not measured.

risks.risk: The scope guard flags or pauses a line sooner, because a rejected repaired attempt's two-round spend and minutes count toward T3 and T5; the reference forecast learns higher cost and time from repaired jobs.
risks.mitigation: Intended and stated in D189 and the CHANGELOG (decision 6). Thresholds are estimates to be tuned (scope_guard.rs:32) and are not retuned without repaired-job data; a repaired attempt that lands gives T3 and T5 None; a near-complete rejection keeps its targeted retry. Two scope pins and the landing-score assertions show the figures; forecasts themselves are untouched.

risks.risk: A round-two stop before a verdict loses round one's verdict, candidate or files, or leaves round two's progress note, kept-work directory or resume mark.
risks.mitigation: Round one's candidate, Verification, happened state and files are cloned before round two and restored when round two returns Ok with no Verification; round two's kept-work directory is removed; the mark was removed before round two and `settle_resume_marks` removes any later one for a Rejected job. The three stop cases and the direct restore test cover it. A hold (error return) keeps the existing hold behaviour.

risks.risk: Recognising Athena's own findings by text can drift if `judge`'s wording changes.
risks.mitigation: The not-assessed evidence and misread summary are shared consts used by `judge`; the two `format!` findings are matched by prefix and suffix consts and `repair_recognisers_match_what_judge_writes` runs the real `judge` for each, so a wording change fails a test instead of silently starting or stopping repairs.

risks.risk: The same failure class can still occur on a resumed-candidate path, a nested run, or a job whose budget or disk cannot pay for round two. A repaired job that passes keeps the first verdict only as text in a verifier invocation's detail.
risks.mitigation: Not repaired and said so in D189 and the CHANGELOG; the budget and disk skips print a `repair     skipped:` line so the stored event shows the repair was considered. Extending to resumed candidates needs a producer snapshot and worktree guard in the resume path, a separate change. A typed first-round record is named as follow-up.

risks.risk: The verifier's findings may be wrong, so a repair can churn the work.
risks.mitigation: The repair only gives information; the verdict is still computed by `judge`, unchanged. The always-fail bound test shows a stubborn verifier ends after one extra round. Misread-only, unassessed-only and (when the verifier passed) D43-only verdicts spend no round.

risks.risk: Throughput's check minutes and busy time read slightly low for repaired jobs, because round two's checks replace round one's in the stored Verification.
risks.mitigation: D189 and the CHANGELOG say so; the landing test pins first_pass == 0 and both rounds' producer and verifier minutes.
